The fix is to URL-encode the display_id so the `/` becomes `%2F`.

transcript.content: Now I have a clear understanding of the issue. The problem is in `yt_dlp/extractor/sportdeutschland.py`. When the URL contains multiple path segments (e.g., `deutscherbadmintonverband/bwf-tour-1-runde-feld-1-yonex-gainward-german-open-2022-0`), the `display_id` captures the full path including the `/`. This is then directly concatenated into the API URL, causing a 404 because the `/` in the display_id is interpreted as a path separator rather than as part of the permalink identifier. The fix is to URL-encode the display_id before inserting it into the API URL.
